premise.claim: Deleting an RBG with the default background propagation makes the RBG object disappear at once while its workload stays behind, still controlled by the old UID; a same-named RBG created inside that window finds the leftover by name and ConstructRoleStatus reads the leftover's readyReplicas, so the RBG can go Ready=True on a workload left by its predecessor.
premise.reportedComponent: pkg/reconciler workload reconcilers (RoleInstanceSet/Deployment/StatefulSet/LeaderWorkerSet) + RBG status construction
premise.evidence: On base (7ed1860c) TestVerifyP0LeftoverReadinessInherited FAILS: ConstructRoleStatus returns ReadyReplicas=1 from a leftover RIS controlled by a previous incarnation's UID, CheckWorkloadReady returns true, and Reconciler writes over it without error. Refined by the integration layer: on a real apiserver the base write path actually fails with 422 'Only one reference can have Controller set to true' (results/integration-base.txt), so the silent damage on base is the status/readiness/dependency reads, exactly the claimed symptom. See results/unit-base.txt.
